title: Launch a role headless, with its opening prompt read from a file

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL — round 1. Audited 62c6220 on branch devteam2/sprint-11, in the worktree at /Users/chrishobbs/Programming/fully-completely-devteam2-sprint-11. Sprint file read fresh there immediately before this verdict. Worktree working tree clean.

The code is good. Two things stop it being a PASS: the sprint's own stated deliverable is absent, and there is one demonstrated dead end in the new credential precondition. Neither is a failure of care — Req 5 was flagged honestly rather than faked, which is the behaviour the sprint's Risks section specifically hoped for.

TREE NOTE, worth one line because it is sprint 7 paying off: running status from the main checkout returned "No state file for sprint 11 in /Users/chrishobbs/Programming/fully-completely (branch: main)". That message told me instantly I was in the wrong tree instead of letting me report sprint 11 as never started. That is the exact four-wrong-readings defect sprint 7 fixed, working. Audited and recorded in the worktree.

================================================================
FINDING 1 (blocking) — REQ 5, THE SPRINT'S STATED DELIVERABLE, IS NOT DONE
================================================================

Req 5's own words: "Discover the six per-role opening prompts by running them. **This is the sprint's deliverable; the flag is the easy half.**" Its criterion: "this cannot be cleared by reading." Team Assignments: "Req 5 is the bulk of the work."

There are no six prompts. Nothing was derived from a headless run, and I am not marking that against Dev Team: the blocker is a missing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, confirmed empirically here too, and the user authorized building the rest. Flagging it openly instead of writing six plausible prompts from a desk is exactly what the sprint's Risks section asked QA1 to watch for, and the honest outcome is better than the fabricated one. But user authorization to proceed is not the same fact as the requirement being met, and this gate records what is true.

WHY THIS IS A CONDITIONAL AND SPRINT 10'S REQ 6 WAS NOT. In sprint 10 the blocker was a Windows machine — nobody at any gate in this environment could clear it, so a CONDITIONAL would have created an unclearable precondition with no recovery path, which this framework has a named rule against. This one is different in the way that matters: an API key and a spend authorization are things the USER can supply, today, from here. There is a real, named, clearable path. That is what makes CONDITIONAL the correct instrument rather than a punishment.

It also costs nothing. The sprint is blocked from shipping anyway — Dependencies hold it until 0.1.10 ships and the registry freeze lifts — and it is already parked at dev_build, where this verdict leaves it. There is no schedule cost to being accurate here, which is precisely when accuracy is cheapest and least excusable to skip.

WHAT CLEARS IT: a credential and a spend decision from the user, then the six runs, then the fixed-vs-template determination Req 5 explicitly asks for ("Answer explicitly whether these are fixed per role or templates parameterized by the work — a headless QA1 needs to know which sprint it is auditing"). That question is unanswered and it is the substantive half.

DO NOT ROUTE THIS TO LIVEQA AS A SUBSTITUTE. LiveQA's criterion says "This is Req 5's verification" — verification of six prompts that do not exist yet is not verification, it is LiveQA doing the discovery under a different name. Req 5 gets done here, then LiveQA verifies it.

================================================================
FINDING 2 (blocking, small) — THE CREDENTIAL PRECONDITION IS A DEAD END FOR apiKeyHelper
================================================================

run-role.js:189. Demonstrated, not argued:

  env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY node scripts/launcher/run-role.js qa1 --headless --prompt-file <path>
  -> ERROR: ...Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and re-run, or configure apiKeyHelper via --settings
     (this check does not detect that case, only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY).
     exit 1

Three things are wrong with that, and they compound:
  1. It is a hard fail() with exit 1 and there is no bypass flag. A project authenticating via apiKeyHelper — which the pinned notes confirm is a first-class supported --bare credential source, not an exotic one — cannot use headless at all.
  2. The message offers "configure apiKeyHelper via --settings" as the remedy, and doing that changes nothing, because the check reads only process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. The user follows the instruction and hits the identical error.
  3. --settings is not plumbed through anywhere. headlessLaunchArgs builds ['--agent', id, '--agents', json, '-p', '--output-format', 'json', '--bare', prompt] — grepped, there is no --settings pass-through in this file at all. So even a user who knows what they are doing has no way to supply it through this launcher. The remedy the message names does not exist on this code path.

The code comment calls this "this warning" (run-role.js:186) while the code is a hard exit 1. The comment misdescribes its own severity.

This is Req 4's own failure mode turned around: the requirement is "fails legibly without them", and this fails illegibly WITH them. It is also, again, a precondition the role that hits it cannot clear.

REQUIRED FIX, and the shape is your call: either drop the precondition and let --bare's own failure surface (the pinned notes confirm it is well-formed and legible — is_error true, "Not logged in · Please run /login" — and this sprint's Out of Scope says we emit and do not parse, so nothing here needs to inspect it), or make it a stderr warning rather than a hard fail, or plumb --settings through and detect apiKeyHelper. What must not survive is a hard block whose stated remedy the code rejects.

================================================================
EVERYTHING ELSE — VERIFIED, AND MOSTLY VERY GOOD
================================================================

REQ 2 — MET, and this is the one the criterion warned a diff would hide, so I did not read it. Traced every write path first: run-role.js contains exactly two console calls, both console.error (fail() at :49, the --restart line at :276); the probe uses stdio:'ignore'; the child uses stdio:'inherit'. agents.js, prompts.js, claude-cmd.js, session.js and auth.js contain zero stdout writes between them.
Then ran it, with a fake claude on PATH printing an envelope to stdout and noise to stderr, capturing the two streams to separate files:
    stdout: {"type":"result","is_error":false,"result":"pong","total_cost_usd":0}   PARSES CLEANLY
    stderr: held the noise, nothing else leaked
    --restart path: stdout PARSES CLEANLY there too
The named offender is fixed and the fix is belt-and-braces — headless returns before the restart branch is reachable at all, and the line was moved to stderr anyway. That is the right instinct for a line whose whole failure mode is "somebody later routes into it".

REQ 1 — MET, and I read it looking for the loophole specifically. Headless goes through the same spawnClaude() and the same child_process.spawn() the interactive path already used; it is one OS process running one role, and there is no path by which a role invokes another. The comment states the CLAUDE.md prohibition as the reason rather than leaving it implicit, which is what Req 1 actually asked for.

REQ 3 — MET in substance, and the substance is what matters. All three failure modes name the file or the missing flag:
    missing file -> "Could not read --prompt-file '<path>': ENOENT... Headless mode needs the opening prompt in a real, readable file."
    empty file   -> "--prompt-file '<path>' is empty. Headless mode needs a real opening prompt."
    no flag      -> "--headless requires --prompt-file <path>."
Note for the record: read literally, "the prompt never transits argv" is not true — it is the last element of the child's spawn argv. Read against its own stated rationale (shell command-substitution), it is fully satisfied: an array-based spawn never goes through a shell, and the flag this script exposes is --prompt-file, so no external caller is invited to concatenate free text into a command line. The comment makes exactly this distinction and makes it correctly. I am not raising it; a criterion is satisfied by its purpose, and I would rather say so than pretend the literal wording was met.

REQ 4's FACTUAL BASIS — CHECKED AGAINST PRIMARY SOURCE, as the criterion demands. I read /Users/chrishobbs/Programming/Fifty_Mission_Cap/metering/output-format-json-notes.md at 39a12fd directly, not from this sprint file or the handoff. It says what is claimed: --bare "strictly requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or apiKeyHelper — OAuth and keychain auth are explicitly not read", and an unauthenticated --bare attempt produced is_error true with "Not logged in · Please run /login" while the envelope stayed well-formed with the same top-level shape, zeroed values and no modelUsage. --bare is passed unconditionally with no opt-out, so headless cannot inherit the operator's OAuth session. The isolation half of Req 4 is correct; only the precondition (Finding 2) is wrong.

REQ 6 — MET, and it is a runnable check rather than a claim. The argv builders are pure and exported, and I asserted against them myself rather than trusting the suite: freshLaunchArgs produces exactly the pre-sprint shape, byte-identical to what 93471c0's inline array built; resumeLaunchArgs produces ['--agent','qa1','--resume',uuid] for a normal role and appends devTeam2ResumePrompt only for dev-team-2 — I got that assertion wrong on my first pass (expected 4 elements, it is correctly 5) and the code was right, not me. Guarding main() with require.main === module is the correct way to make this testable without changing CLI behaviour.

REQ 7 — MET, read cold. Both files name the trigger characters explicitly ("backticks, `$`, or code of any kind"), state the action (write to a file, use --notes-file), cite the real incident rather than a hypothetical, and tell the reader not to improvise a shorter direct invocation that skips the command file's own pattern. That last clause is the one that will actually prevent recurrence.

REQ 9 — MET, run not read. 99 OK lines, ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED.
verify-tarball.sh: TARBALL VERIFICATION PASSED, launcher files match live source, sprint data clean, baseline table present.

REQ 8 — HELD, CORRECTLY, AND THE SPRINT FILE CONTRADICTS ITSELF. package.json is 0.1.10. Req 8 says bump to 0.1.11; Dependencies says "Hold the version bump until ship time if 0.1.10 has not gone out yet — Req 8 and sprint 10's Req 7 edit the same line." 0.1.10 has not shipped. Dev followed Dependencies, which is the right call, and the acceptance criterion for Req 8 is therefore unsatisfiable as written today. Recording it as a specification contradiction rather than a defect: Master Controller should reconcile the two, and Req 8 must be done before this ships regardless.

================================================================
INFORMATIONAL — NOT REQUIRED FIXES
================================================================

1. QUANTIFIED CEILING NOBODY HAS NOTICED. The --agents payload puts the entire persona body in the child's argv. Measured all six: master-controller 10,778 chars, qa1 9,718, dev-team-2 9,493, pipeman 8,925, liveqa 8,418, dev-team-1 8,397. Full argv worst case ~10,845 chars against Windows' 32,767-char CreateProcess limit, leaving ~21,900 shared with the opening prompt. Fine today. Agent files grow every sprint — this sprint alone added to two of them — and sprint 10 just made Windows a first-class target, so this is a real budget with a real limit and it is currently uncounted. If a role's persona and its opening prompt ever approach that together, headless fails on Windows only, which is the exact platform-asymmetric failure class sprint 10 existed to end.

2. The interactive path's check ORDER changed: the operator auth check used to run before the agent-file existence check and now runs after it. Only observable when both fail at once, where the user now sees the agent-file error instead of the auth error. Not a regression in function and Req 6's criterion is about the path still working, which it demonstrably does. Worth knowing it moved.

3. Unverified and correctly flagged by Dev: whether `model` inside the --agents JSON is honored or silently ignored. Needs a credentialed run — same blocker as Req 5, and it should be answered in the same pass rather than as a separate errand.

4. For sequencing, observed in the main checkout, not this worktree: sprint 10's QA1 PASS bookkeeping (registry.json and state/sprint-10.json) is still uncommitted on main. Under sprint 9's release ordering that is fine and arguably correct, but somebody should know it is sitting there before shipping 0.1.10.

CODE QUALITY

Test coverage: 99 passing; the CLI-level headless tests use a fake claude on PATH, so they cost nothing and still exercise the real process boundary — the right design for this.
Error handling: every headless failure names the file, the flag, or the missing credential. fail() is stderr-only throughout.
Standards: agentBody() reuses parseFrontmatter's own regex match rather than a second copy, with the reason stated; readAgentMeta gained a field additively; pure argv builders extracted rather than duplicated. The persona can never be described differently by the two launch paths, which was the right thing to guarantee.
Security: the --prompt-file design is correct and the comment reasons about it accurately, including being clear that this file's own spawn is not the exposure.
Reporting accuracy: the handoff's claims all held up — zero console.log, tests green, tarball passing, and the repointed baseline tests were repointed for the stated reason.

RECOMMENDATION

Fix Finding 2 (one function, your call on shape), and get Req 5 done once the user supplies a credential and authorizes the spend — including the fixed-vs-template answer, and item 3 above while the credentials are live. Then come back for round 2. Do not touch anything else: Req 2's stdout discipline and Req 1's process separation are both correct and I do not want them disturbed by an unrelated fix.

Nothing ships regardless until 0.1.10 is out and the freeze lifts, so there is time to do Req 5 properly rather than fast.
